title: Work out a trigonometric value in radians with Calculator

source.licence: CC-BY-NC-4.0; ported by reference (our own instruction, setup and checks; no source text copied)
source.changes: Instruction written in our own words. The function and angle are a param; the source's sine of pi/6 is one pick, and the others (cosine of pi/3, tangent of pi/4) also need radians and Scientific mode. The source restored an AMI snapshot; here setup quits Calculator and clears its last result, and teardown puts the Mac's own value back. The check reads the same preference as the source (com.apple.calculator LastResultValue), compared to six decimals exactly instead of with grep. The oracle types a division with the same result into Calculator: it proves the check reads a solved state, not that the agent used the trigonometric key.

setup.why: Keep the Mac's own last Calculator result for teardown, quit Calculator and clear the result, so an agent that does nothing leaves no result to read.

instruction: Use the Calculator app to work out {{f.say}}, with the angle in radians, and leave the value as Calculator's result.

checks.why: Calculator's last result (LastResultValue, saved at each = or function key), to six decimals, is {{f.say}} in radians. The same angle in degrees gives another number (0.009138, 0.999833 or 0.013709), so a degrees-mode answer fails. Setup deleted the value, so an agent that does nothing reads empty and fails.

teardown.why: Quit Calculator and put the Mac's own last result back.

oracle.why: Basic mode (Command-1), clear twice, then type a division with the same value and = as a person would.
